chapters.title: Chapter 2: Government-Backed and Fixed Return Options

lessons.title: EPF and VPF: The 80C Benefit Hidden in Your Payslip

children.text: If you are salaried, there is a line on your payslip that quietly does more tax planning than most people do in March. It says "PF" or "EPF Employee Contribution", and every rupee in it counts towards Section 123 (80C). Many salaried people have used half or more of their ₹1.5 lakh limit before they buy a single product. This lesson shows you how to read that line, what changed in 2026, and when it makes sense to put in more through VPF.

children.text: Reading the PF Line on Your Payslip

markDefs.definition: Employees' Pension Scheme: a pension account funded only by part of the employer's contribution. It pays a monthly pension after age 58 and does not count towards your 80C deduction.

children.text: Both you and your employer put in 12% of your PF wages. Your 12% goes entirely into your EPF account. Your employer's 12% is split: 8.33% of wages up to ₹15,000 (a maximum of ₹1,250 a month) goes into the
, and the rest goes into your EPF account.

body.caption: Priyanka, an HR manager in Pune, with PF wages of ₹60,000 a month and an employer that contributes on actual wages

cells: Total going into PF and pension

body.text: Priyanka's ₹86,400 of EPF uses 58% of her ₹1,50,000 limit automatically. Her real 80C gap is only ₹63,600. The employer's share does not count towards 80C, but it is not taxed as salary either, as long as total employer contributions to EPF, NPS and superannuation stay within ₹7.5 lakh a year.

body.title: What Counts?
body.question: Priyanka's employer shows ₹1,72,800 as the yearly total going into PF and pension in her CTC letter. How much of this can she claim under Section 123 (80C)?
body.explanation: Only the employee's own contribution is deducted from her salary and counts under 80C. The employer's share, whether it goes to EPF or EPS, is a separate benefit that never passes through her taxable salary in the first place.

children.text: What Changed in 2026: The 50% Wage Rule

On 29 June 2026, the government notified the Employees' Provident Fund Scheme, 2026 under the Code on Social Security, 2020, replacing the 1952 scheme. The 12% rate did not change. What changed is the base it applies to. PF is now calculated on "wages" as defined in the Code, and if excluded allowances such as HRA and conveyance make up more than 50% of your total pay, the excess is added back to your PF wages.

body.caption: Salary structures loaded with allowances to keep PF low now get part of those allowances pulled back into the PF base.

body.title: Deepak, a consultant in Noida: total monthly pay ₹1,00,000

columns.label: Old basis (basic wages)
points: HRA, conveyance and other excluded allowances: ₹65,000

body.text: The ₹15,000 statutory wage ceiling has not changed. PF is mandatory only on wages up to ₹15,000. Whether your contribution is calculated on your full PF wages or capped at ₹15,000 (₹1,800 a month) depends on your employer's policy, so the 50% rule raises your deduction only if your employer contributes on actual wages. Check your July 2026 payslip onwards to see whether your PF line moved.

body.title: Your Turn: Apply the 50% Rule
body.prompt: Farah works in Bengaluru. Her total monthly pay is ₹80,000: basic + DA of ₹28,000 and excluded allowances of ₹52,000. Her employer contributes on actual wages. Under the EPF Scheme, 2026, what is her yearly employee EPF contribution that counts under Section 123 (80C)?
body.explanation: 50% of ₹80,000 is ₹40,000. Her excluded allowances of ₹52,000 exceed that by ₹12,000, so PF wages become ₹28,000 + ₹12,000 = ₹40,000. Employee EPF is 12% × ₹40,000 = ₹4,800 a month, or ₹57,600 a year. Under the old basis it would have been 12% × ₹28,000 × 12 = ₹40,320.

children.text: VPF: Topping Up at the EPF Rate

Voluntary Provident Fund lets you contribute more than the mandatory 12% into the same EPF account, through payroll. It earns the same 8.25%, counts under Section 123 (80C) along with your regular EPF, and is currently the highest-yielding government-backed option available to salaried employees. Under the 2026 scheme, either you or your employer can reduce or stop voluntary contributions at any time, and your employer is not required to match them.

children.text: Since FY 2021-22, interest on employee contributions (EPF plus VPF) above ₹2.5 lakh in a year is taxable. The limit is ₹5 lakh where the employer does not contribute, as with many government employees. EPFO maintains a separate taxable sub-account for the excess. This rule continues under the Income-tax Act, 2025.

body.title: Quick Check
body.textWithBlank: For a private sector employee whose employer also contributes, interest on yearly employee EPF and VPF contributions above ₹___ lakh is taxable.
body.explanation: The threshold is ₹2.5 lakh when the employer contributes and ₹5 lakh when it does not. Contributions above the threshold still earn 8.25%; only the interest on the excess is taxed.

cards.definition: Universal Account Number: one lifelong number that links every PF account across employers. Always transfer old PF balances into it when you switch jobs.
Withdrawals are tax-free if you have 5 years of continuous service, counting all previous employers whose balances were transferred to your current account.
Becomes taxable: past 80C deductions on your contributions are reversed, and the employer's share and interest are taxed. EPFO deducts 10% TDS if your PAN is linked.
Under 2026 rules, grouped into essential needs, housing needs and special circumstances. Available after 12 months of service, up to 75% of the eligible balance.

cards.term: Final settlement after leaving a job
cards.definition: Requires 12 months of unemployment before the full balance can be withdrawn. Partial access remains available during that time.
Pension balance can be withdrawn only after 36 months, and only if you have less than 10 years of eligible service.

body.title: Scenario: The Sabbatical Withdrawal
body.scenario: Ananya, 27, has worked for 4 years across three employers in Chennai and Bengaluru and has transferred all her PF into one UAN. Her EPF balance is ₹4,20,000. She resigns to take a year-long sabbatical and plans to withdraw everything in the first month to fund travel, since 'it is my money anyway'.
body.prompt: What can Ananya actually withdraw right now, and what would full withdrawal cost her in tax? What would you suggest?
body.modelAnswer: She cannot take a final settlement immediately. Under the 2026 rules, full settlement needs 12 months without employment, although she can access up to 75% of the eligible balance through a partial withdrawal. More importantly, she has only 4 years of continuous service. Withdrawing now makes it taxable: her past 80C deductions on her own contributions are reversed, the employer's share and all interest become taxable, and EPFO deducts 10% TDS if her PAN is linked. If she completes 5 years of service after the sabbatical, the entire balance, including 8.25% interest earned in the meantime, becomes tax-free. A better plan is to fund the sabbatical from savings or a liquid fund, withdraw only what she truly needs, and join her next employer on the same UAN so the service clock keeps counting.

body.title: Your EPF Health Check
steps: Log in to the EPFO member portal with your UAN and confirm your KYC (Aadhaar, PAN, bank account) is complete
Download your passbook and check every previous employer's balance is transferred into your current UAN
Note your employee contribution for the tax year and subtract it from ₹1,50,000 to find your 80C gap
Compare your July 2026 payslip with June 2026 to see whether the 50% wage rule changed your PF deduction
If you still have an 80C gap and value safety, ask HR whether VPF can be started through payroll
Keep total employee contributions under ₹2.5 lakh a year if you want all interest to stay tax-free

body.label: EPFO Member Passbook
body.description: Log in with your UAN to see month-wise employee, employer and pension contributions and interest credited.

points: Only your own EPF contribution counts under Section 123 (80C). The employer's EPF and EPS shares do not.
EPF often fills a large part of the ₹1.5 lakh limit before you invest anything else.
From 29 June 2026, the EPF Scheme, 2026 calculates PF on Code wages, and allowances above 50% of pay are added back to the PF base.
VPF earns the same 8.25% as EPF and counts under 80C, but only interest on total employee contributions up to ₹2.5 lakh a year stays tax-free.
Withdrawals are tax-free after 5 years of continuous service. Earlier withdrawals reverse past deductions and attract TDS.
Transfer PF on every job change so your service clock and tax-free status stay intact.

body.text: This lesson is for educational purposes only and is not tax, legal or investment advice. EPF interest rates are declared yearly, and the EPF Scheme, 2026 is recent; clarificatory circulars may refine how the 50% wage rule and withdrawal limits apply. Confirm your own figures with your employer's HR or payroll team and consult a qualified professional for decisions specific to your situation.
